FHI Bangladesh began activities under the USAIDs Implementing AIDS Prevention and Care (IMPACT) project from 2000 until September 2007 to support interventions for people most vulnerable to HIV. FHI continued to support USAID/Dhakas strategy and the Bangladesh Ministry of Healths priorities by concentrating efforts on groups most vulnerable to HIV. (Bangladesh): The Early Childhood Development Mass Media Activity Sisimpur supports the development of pre-literacy skills and the dissemination of key life skills messages to more than 10 million children aged 3 to 8 through popular television programming. In the coming year, Sisimpur will develop 52 television episodes and broadcast them throughout the year. In support of the goals of the Mission's Country Development and Cooperation Strategy, Sisimpur episodes will deliver child-friendly key messages on the importance of basic health, nutrition and hand washing. To complement the television episodes, the activity will also create and distribute 20 new story books with these key messages to 100 schools, and develop 10 e-learning materials to support the technology initiatives of the Government of Bangladesh. Finally, the activity will build the capacity of the local implementing organization Sesame Workshop Bangladesh to ensure the initiative's future sustainability.The activity supports the U.S. National Security Strategy, the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal Two, and the U.S. Government's mission objective of improved health status in Bangladesh.

title.narrative: Mamoni Maternal and Newborn Care Strengthening Project (MNCSP) Activity

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The MaMoni Maternal and Newborn Care Strengthening Project (MNCSP) will reduce maternal and neonatal mortality and increase contraceptive prevalence by strengthening health systems and facilities to provide quality maternal and newborn health care and postpartum FP and nutrition services. With FY 2022 funds, MaMoni MNCSP will target vulnerable population groups in hard-to-reach geographies with poor maternal and newborn care indicators. This activity will continue to improve health system responsiveness to deliver quality services, improve access and demand for care, strengthen governance, healthy household practices, and the national capacity to scale-up evidence-based care. The activity will support the institutionalization of comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care, management of sick newborns, midwifery care in select district and sub-district health facilities, and will strengthen the capacity of service providers to manage complications and screen for obstetric fistula. The activity will further enhance newborn care at all levels, including essential newborn care through special care newborn units, helping babies breathe, chlorhexidine use for cord care, and kangaroo mother care. The activity will also increase FP services, focusing on postpartum FP. In addition, MaMoni MNCSP will improve the quality of nutrition counseling during pregnancy and lactation and demonstrate early initiation of breastfeeding after birth. The activity will train service providers on these nutrition issues and counsel key family members to support the mother. This activity will contribute to adaptation-indirect (MCH-$600K, FPRH-$300K), micronutrients (Nutri-$80K of which $80K is for micronutrients Vit A) earmarks.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Promoting Advocacy and Rights (PAR) activity works to strengthen the capacity of civil-society to advocate for improved democratic governance and establish partnerships to improve government responsiveness to citizens' needs. USAID provides local organizations with grants to build their advocacy capabilities and supports the advocacy efforts of coalitions of civil society organizations (CSOs) and local government agencies to address community problems, such as gender-based violence, drug addiction, environmental pollution, and unplanned urbanization. The advocacy model involves an initial community survey in which CSOs and citizens prioritize social concerns or community problems. CSOs then form a coalition of stakeholders, including local government agencies, and then develop a charter of action to collectively advocate for change and to address a specific social issue or community problem. USAID will continue to provide CSOs with technical support so they can conduct a variety of strategic advocacy campaigns with the goal of increasing the confidence of citizens in their local government's ability to resolve community problems. USAID will also provide CSOs with digital security tools to help them learn about their legal rights and compliance responsibilities. This IM contributes to meeting the required GBV ($200K), Child Marriage ($1M), DRG ($1.7M), and Freedom of Expression ($300K) earmarks. This activity will be in line with the State-USAID Integrated Country Strategy (ICS) Mission Goal Two and the U.S. government development objective of enhanced opportunities for an inclusive, healthy, educated society, and a robust economy.. .

title.narrative: Accelerating Universal Access to Family Planning (AUAFP) - Shukhi Jibon Activity

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Accelerating Universal Access to Family Planning (AUAFP) activity will work with the GoB to increase access to and quality of family planning (FP) services to improve the contraceptive prevalence rate for modern methods, including long-acting reversible contraceptives. AUAFP will also help to address the reproductive health (RH) needs of adolescents and reduce the rate of adolescent pregnancies. With FY 2022 funds, USAID will implement AUAFP at the national level, with FP training institutes and public and private sector service providers in four divisions, covering half the country and focusing on the most in-need and vulnerable populations. AUAFP will improve the capacity of FP training institute trainers to use competency-based and adult learning approaches, teach supervisors to adopt mentorship and supportive supervision skills, and integrate adolescent care and gender into their training programs to expand the skills of health service providers. AUAFP will strengthen service readiness interventions by ensuring focus facilities meet the required standards to deliver quality FP and RH services. USAID will apply innovative demand-side approaches, including digital and social media, focused on adolescents and youth. The activity will increase the utilization and track the use of FP services by underserved groups, including ethnic and religious minorities, ready-made garment workers, and people with disabilities. AUAFP will address the underlying issues perpetuating gender-based violence and strengthen clinical services to care for survivors. This activity will contribute to the adaptation-indirect (FPRH-$300K) earmark.

(Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Nutrition activity improves nutrition outcomes of children under five, pregnant and lactating women, and adolescent girls. The activity's technical assistance and social and behavioral communication interventions will increase access to nutritious, diverse, and safe diets; strengthen social and economic empowerment; and improve adoption of good water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) practices by rural households. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will facilitate private and public sector partners to train service providers, market actors, rural households, and other critical stakeholders. These training will build the knowledge and skills needed to increase the demand and supply of nutritious, diverse, and safe foods, which will lead to increased dietary diversity. The activity will continue to empower women and adolescents to engage in economic activities, adopt healthy behaviors, and participate in household decision-making. The activity will work with private companies and local entrepreneurs to create awareness in rural households and to offer improved sanitation, safe drinking water, and hygiene solutions. title.narrative: Livelihood Improvement and Forest Enrichment(GREEN LIFE)

description.narrative: Greening Environment through Livelihood Improvement and Forest Enrichment(GREEN LIFE).This activity will strengthen the co-management organizations (CMOs) of the Inani National Park (2,200 ha) and provide livelihood development support to 1,800 households. Using the farmer field school (FFS) approach, the selected beneficiaries will be provided with technical skills training on improving farming practices. They will also be provided with critical input support and cash grants to their Revolving Loan Fund (RLF). The activity will build capacity of the co-management organizations as well as the local staff of the Bangladesh Forest Department (BFD). To reduce the use of firewood, the activity will promote a supply chain of alternative fuel solutions such as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and retained heat cookers (RHCs) at the household level. For bulk users like restaurants and orphanages, it will share the cost of customized improved cook-stoves (ICS). It will also test a locally fabricated simple burner (kero-gas burner). In addition, the activity will distribute seedlings of fast growing and high biomass yielding fuel wood tree species among the local communities. The activity will also promote the production of endangered native tree species of the region by providing training to private nursery owners of Coxs Bazar district. In addition to building organizational development and management capacities of CMOs in Ukhia, the activity will enhance the capacity of the applicant in two important areas: (a) fundraising and (b) advanced applications of geo-spatial technologies. This capacity development will help the applicant to sustain its operations and to contribute towards forest and biodiversity conservation in Bangladesh.

(Bangladesh): Bangladesh is an important source, consumer, and transit point for illegally traded wildlife. The Interagency Agreement (IAA) between USAID and the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) International Criminal Investigative Technical Assistance Program capitalizes on the DOJ's unique relationship with the law enforcement bodies responsible for investigating wildlife crimes, and the judiciary responsible for trying criminals. This IAA improves the status of endangered and protected wildlife species by reducing illegal capture, killing, trade, and consumption of wildlife through strengthening the GoB's enforcement, investigative capacity, and interagency coordination. ICITAP will build the technical capacity of police; forestry, environment, fisheries, and customs authorities and personnel; as well as border guards and coast guards. With FY 2024 funds, ICITAP will coordinate with USAID's Wildlife Protection activity to provide training on wildlife crime investigations, analysis, detection, prosecution, and awareness. title.narrative: FTF Bangladesh Agricultural Infrastructure Development Activity (BAIDA)

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Agricultural Infrastructure Development activity improves rural infrastructure in southern Bangladesh, especially rural roads, markets, collection centers, and drainage systems. The activity coordinates with other FTF activities to identify high-impact rural infrastructure projects that reduce travel time for farmers bringing their goods to market, improve the sanitation and safety of rural markets, and enhance the conditions of collection centers to reduce food waste. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will improve rural market roads, drainage systems, market centers and collection hubs to boost agricultural productivity, increase production, and strengthen food security. The activity works with local institutions to ensure the long-term sustainable maintenance of completed infrastructure projects, including local governments and market management committees. This activity supports the Global Food Security Strategy and the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan goals two and three. (Bangladesh): Bangladesh is a source, destination, and transit country for forced labor and human trafficking. Widespread poverty, unemployment, corruption, poor governance, porous borders, and traditional gender inequities fuel trafficking. The 2024 Department of State Trafficking in Persons (TIP) report kept Bangladesh at Tier Two, stressing the urgent need for the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) to allocate more resources to counter trafficking and fully comply with the Trafficking Victims Protection Act (TVPA). The high rate of child marriage (CM) is concerning, with 52 percent of girls marrying before 18, leaving them vulnerable to trafficking.With FY 2024 funds, USAID's Fight Slavery and Trafficking in Persons (FSTIP) activity will expand partnerships with civil society and the private sector to strengthen comprehensive protection mechanisms for those at risk and survivors of trafficking and CM. FSTIP will engage the GoB, youth, civil society organizations, and community members to prevent human rights violations and raise awareness of TIP and CM. It will also enhance judicial and law enforcement capacity to bring perpetrators to justice, supporting the GoB-led National Plan of Action and the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act of 2012. FSTIP will also support the implementation of several recommendations outlined in the 2024 TIP report for GoB.This IM contributes to the Women, Peace and Security earmark ($200k), Trafficking in Persons ($300k), and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support ($100k). The activity is in line with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 1.1 - Bangladesh is more capable of protecting its sovereignty, population, and borders, combating terrorism, and countering violent extremism and USAID's CDCS Mission Development Objective 1 - Democracy Strengthened for an Inclusive Society.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): While Bangladesh's garment industry has largely recovered, high post-pandemic inflation has severely impacted garment factory workers, worsening inequalities, especially for women in the ready-made garments (RMG) sector. Although the RMG sector is the second-largest economic sector in Bangladesh, studies show a continuing decline in female RMG workers, who now make up 54 percent of the workforce. With FY 2024 funds, the W-GDP Women Thrive in Bangladesh (Thrive) activity will support over 100,000 female RMG workers in developing professional and leadership skills, mainly within PVH Corporation supply chain factories and surrounding communities. The White House Women's Global Development and Prosperity initiative has allocated $3 million for the project, with USAID/Bangladesh providing additional funds. This initiative aims to reduce the gender gap in RMG factories and strengthen women's advocacy and negotiation skills, advancing their rights and leadership. Thrive will operate in Dhaka, Gazipur, Mymensingh, Kishoreganj, Chattogram, and Narayanganj. The activity will enhance the livelihoods and well-being of workers, particularly female workers, by increasing efficiency and job retention. It will create career progression opportunities for women by fostering employer buy-in and building a more resilient female workforce. Additionally, it will connect women to other employment opportunities, helping to mitigate the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic and other future challenges.This IM contributes to the Women's Leadership earmark ($200k) and Private Sector Engagement ($200k). It is in line with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Goal 2 - Bangladesh is committed to democracy, transparency, pluralism, tolerance, good governance, and respect for human rights, and supports USAID's CDCS Mission Development Objective 1 - Democracy Strengthened for an Inclusive Society.

title.narrative: FTF Bangladesh Livestock and Nutrition Activity

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Livestock and Nutrition activity aims to sustainably increase the productivity of livestock, as well as the marketability and consumption of livestock products. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will facilitate productivity-enhancing technologies and practices such as processing and preservation of fodder for year-round livestock feeding; support enhanced dairy processing and preservation into diversified nutritious products, especially in rural areas; promote the consumption of diversified and safe livestock products; and collaborate with appropriate agencies, such as the Department of Livestock Services, the Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute, and the Food and Agriculture Organization Emergency Center for Transboundary Diseases. The activity will facilitate access to credit, including microfinance. The activity will adopt a market systems approach and engage the private sector to ensure the sustainability of its interventions, contributing to improved food security in Bangladesh. The activity will promote climate-smart technologies and practices, such as saline and flood-tolerant fodder varieties along the coastal belt of the country. It will strengthen the capacity of artificial insemination technicians to provide services that will improve livestock breeds, which are able to withstand environmental shocks and stresses. The activity aligns with the three objectives of the U.S. government's Global Food Security Strategy. description.narrative: (Bangladesh): USAID's Bangladesh Advancing Development and Growth through Energy (BADGE) activity promotes energy security and resilience through improved access to affordable, dependable, and sustainable energy systems. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will provide technical assistance, advisory services, and capacity building training to public and private sector players, and develop tools, strategy documents, and recommendation papers for government agencies. It will conduct multiple policy assessments and make policy recommendations for building an enabling environment suitable for scaling up renewable energy use in Bangladesh. This will include a review of the national energy policy, private power generating policy, guidelines, and other pertinent global renewable energy policies and practices. The activity will also take a Gender Equity and Social Inclusion (GESI) approach to planning, implementing, and making decisions about its interventions. The energy sector remains a male-dominated industry globally. YouthRISE will help host community youth build resilience by ensuring that underlying economic grievances are addressed, strengthening their skills for constructive engagement, and addressing harmful gender norms. With FY 2022 funds, USAID will enhance the capacity of local youth, with the goal of developing social and economic resilience in host communities. USAID will provide livelihood training to 1,200 youth coupled with life/leadership skills to help address conflict in their communities. With FY 2022 funds, this activity will also engage youth in the informal justice system, and involve 3,000 youth in events, training, and activities designed to build mass support for peace and reconciliation.This activity is in line with the Integrated Country Strategy (ICS) Mission Goals One and the U.S. government development objective of strengthened resilience to shocks and stressors. With FY 2024 funds, in collaboration with the Government of Bangladesh, this activity will enhance learning opportunities for all primary school children by providing technical assistance on disability inclusion, and developing and implementing a comprehensive, scalable model for inclusive education in public schools. USAID will focus on building a sustainable model that provides inclusive education in public schools by addressing students' diverse learning needs; training teachers in identifying, supporting, and teaching children with disabilities; and improving awareness of the value of inclusive education among parents, caregivers, and communities. The activity will partner with the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education to strengthen service delivery of inclusive education and create inclusive school environments for all primary school children. This activity aligns with the USAID Education Policy priority of ensuring that children, particularly the most marginalized and vulnerable, have increased access to safe, quality education. A Project Ekota (Unity): From Invisible to Visible funded by USAID creates a space for People Living with Disability (PLWD) for claiming their rights and justice and an accountability mechanism for relevant duty-bearing institutions to render better services to PLWD. The barriers that PLWD face are manifold societal, institutional and infrastructural. Although there are multiple factors, it has appeared that inability to access basic services and resources by disabled people at large is a great obstacle to their overall development. These barriers to accessibility entail education, health, safety-nets, employment, development activities and legal justice. The project aims to leave behind a score of self-managed Disabled Peoples Organisations (DPOs) to continue claiming and realising rights and legal justice in a sustainable and replicable manner. A more sensitised government service providers will be in place in public service delivery provisions. More opportunities will be created to engage PLWD with self-employment or paid work. Project Objectives: To enhance all basic quality services for PLWD, particularly for women and girls.

title.narrative: Advancing Women’s Rights of Access to Information in Bangladesh (AWRTI-2)

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): In Bangladesh, the most marginalized populations face restricted access to information, with women disproportionately affected. Corruption thrives in an environment characterized by secrecy, lack of transparency, weak accountability, and barriers to information, which fuels corruption. USAID's Advancing Women's Rights to Access Information in Bangladesh (AWRTI-2) activity promotes access to information as a means to combat corruption. This initiative will empower citizens to file requests for non-controversial data, thereby building a framework for transparent governance.With FY 2024 funds, the activity will provide training to women in the community on how to access government-held information and work with local communities to raise awareness about the challenges women face when exercising their right to access information. The program will also collaborate with civil society organizations focused on women's rights and economic empowerment to enhance women's understanding of the 2009 Right to Information Act (RTI). AWRTI-2 will also partner with Government of Bangladesh ministries to train designated information officers, aiming to mitigate gender disparities in information dissemination practices and enhance their capacity for effective RTI implementation. The initiative will ensure gender-sensitive implementation of the RTI law, making the government more transparent and open to public scrutiny, which is expected to strengthen anti-corruption efforts.It will create an evidence base for the government to develop better-informed policies that contribute to the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 2.2 - Citizen confidence in governance institutions increases. The overall goal of reducing corruption through increased public-led accountability directly aligns with USAID's CDCS MO1 - Democracy strengthened for an inclusive society. This IM contributes to the Women's Leadership earmark ($200k) and Anti-Corruption ($300k).

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): Youth comprise 35 percent of Bangladesh's population and have the potential to significantly contribute to Bangladesh's socio-economic success. Historically, youth have not been empowered to maximize their potential and continue to experience high unemployment (13.8 percent) due to lack of soft and technical skills. Traditional gender and social norms also hinder youth workforce participation across sectors. To address this, the USAID Bijoyee (Winner) activity will elevate youths' ability to effectively contribute to the economy and society. With FY 2024 funds, Bijoyee will provide youth with skills to better access economic opportunities and strengthen the organizational capacity of local youth and youth-led organizations to serve more youth in the future. This activity will equip youth with industry-demanded soft skills, increase their ability to better access wage and self-employment opportunities, increase youth participation in civic action, and support young Bangladeshis in their journey towards being global citizens. USAID will partner with the Government of Bangladesh and the private sector to transform the youth-serving ecosystem in line with localization principles and shift power to youth. Bijoyee will benefit youth from diverse backgrounds, prioritizing those not currently in education, employment, or training and encourage civic engagement and advocacy on topics such as addressing climate change and for changes to restrictive traditional gender and social norms. The activity aligns with CDCS DO Two and Three and ICS MO 3.1 Improved human capital, particularly in health and education. Funding will contribute to the Basic Education ($625,802) earmark with Girls in Areas of Conflict ($625,802), Gender Equality/Women's Empowerment - Secondary ($ 375k), Gender Based Violence ($250k), and Private Sector Engagement ($125,160) attributions.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .Bangladesh suffers from a dysfunctional rule of law system, which negatively impacts progress toward achieving its democracy, development, and good governance goals. Formal justice institutions are complex and fraught with delays, leading to low levels of citizen confidence and trust in the judiciary. Marginalized communities, in particular, face inadequate access to justice. USAID's Ain Shohayota (Legal Aid) activity will improve citizens' access to justice, strengthen the judicial system, and enhance services for the poor and vulnerable populations. This activity will promote people-centered justice through increased public participation, inclusivity, and data-driven approaches to strengthen the justice system...With FY 2024 funds, Ain Shohayota will increase demand for responsive justice services, promote pro bono legal assistance, and build and utilize an evidence base to enhance justice services. The activity will collaborate with government ministries and the judiciary on effective case management and court administration systems are in place. This initiative will strengthen alternative dispute resolution mechanisms, such as mediation, at the local level. This activity will partner with local civil society organizations to promote people-centered justice by raising awareness of human rights and legal aid services, particularly among vulnerable youth. To fill a gap in legal education, the activity will encourage law students to understand and provide legal aid and pro bono legal services through an internship program with six universities..This IM contributes to the Women, Peace and Security earmark ($100k), Private Sector Engagement ($100k)k and Youth in Development ($100k) issues. The activity is in line with the Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective 2.2 - Citizen confidence in governance institutions increases and USAID's CDCS Mission Development Objective 1 - Democracy strengthened for an inclusive society.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): In Bangladesh, over 90 percent of students in grades 11 and 12 are enrolled in private high schools. The number of students enrolled in higher secondary education increased by 4.9 percent from 2016 to 2020, reflecting a positive trend. However, despite the increase in enrollment, the quality of higher secondary education has not kept pace. The Government of Bangladesh has identified several gaps that impact student learning: (1) the lack of teacher capacity to effectively teach and prepare students with 21st century skills; (2) the lack of appropriate teacher training materials; (3) inadequate teacher training institutions; (4) soft and transferable skills that are not taught in schools; and (6) education officers and supervisors who lack the required capacity to manage the system and support teachers. USAID's Higher Secondary Education activity will follow a system strengthening approach to improve the quality of teaching for Bangladeshi secondary school students to reduce these gaps. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will train teachers, principals, vice principals, and education officers on instructional, management, and supervision skills; develop a comprehensive online learning management system; and pilot innovative approaches to enhance learning of marginalized and disadvantaged students, especially for girls in areas of conflict, such as communities hosting refugees. It will also work with relevant government agencies to enhance teachers' instruction and management skills. The activity aligns with CDCS development objective three and ICS MO 3.1 Improved human capital, particularly in health and education. Funding for this activity contributes to the Basic Education ($2m) earmark with Girls in Areas of Conflict ($1.46m), and Private Sector Engagement ($65,000) attributions.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Quality Assurance Support Activity provides quality assurance surveillance, construction monitoring services, and other technical support for USAID's infrastructure investments. This activity ensures that infrastructure implemented through the FTF Bangladesh Agricultural Infrastructure Development activity is cost effective, sustainable, and complies with applicable national or international standards and codes and engineering best practices. The activity will utilize FY 2024 funds to provide services and support such as reviewing plans, technical reports, and designs; periodic monitoring of construction; third-party quality verification; and commissioning support to ensure that the FTF Bangladesh Agricultural Infrastructure Development activity complies with design specifications, including quality assurance, safety implementation, schedules, guarantees, and other contract terms and conditions. The activity supports the Global Food Security Strategy. Funding for the activity contributes to the Global Food Security ($800,000) earmark.

title.narrative: FTF Bangladesh Inclusive Access to Finance Activity

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Inclusive Access to Finance activity will facilitate increased access to finance for agricultural micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and smallholder farmers. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will work on the supply and demand sides of the market for financing. On the supply side, the activity will partner with banks, microfinance institutions, non-bank financial institutions, and village savings and loan associations to create new blended finance products for target populations and sectors. The activity will also work with financial institutions to develop new loan products tailored to the needs of USAID's target populations, and to strengthen their knowledge of USAID's priority sectors. On the demand side of the market, USAID will help prospective borrowers become more creditworthy through targeted training and assistance. The activity will make special efforts to increase lending to priority populations and sectors, including women and youth, first-time borrowers, and farmers and businesses investing in climate-smart agricultural techniques. As a result of the investments facilitated by the activity, MSMEs and farmers will increase their productivity, invest in climate-smart agricultural techniques, and become more incorporated into the formal financial system. The activity supports the Global Food Security Strategy. Funding for the activity contributes to the Global Food Security ($3.7m), Gender Equality and Women Empowerment Secondary ($700k), Private Sector Engagement ($1m), MSME (300k) directives and key issues.

(Bangladesh): USAID's Bangladesh America Maitree Activity (BAMA) is an integrated activity that is grounded in locally driven strategies to strengthen the capacity of Bangladesh's civil society partners and promote broad-based, inclusive, and sustainable development. Using FY 2024 funds, Maitree will issue small grants to Bangladeshi NGOs through its flexible grant-making facility and offer a range of capacity strengthening options to qualified local partners based on participatory organizational assessments that will direct the technical and organizational capacity strengthening support. The activity will also strengthen the capacity of the NGO/CSO network in Bangladesh for advocacy efforts on shared agendas.This activity will advance all four development objectives of the CDCS and cover all technical sectors that the Mission implements. This is the Mission's integrated initiative on localization. Funding for the activity contributes to the Global Food Security ($2,000,000).

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): USAID's ClimAct Activity will strengthen the policy environment and governance structure, making it favorable for transformational changes in key systems aiming at net-zero emissions and a climate-resilient Bangladesh. This activity aims to catalyze long-term systemic shifts in Bangladesh's economy, institutions, and governance structures through interventions such as enabling policy development, facilitating technology transfer, bolstering climate research, and catalyzing the scaling of climate actions. With FY 2024 funds, the activity will develop local-level adaptation actions in selected climate hot spots, enhance local government institutions' capacity for climate planning and monitoring, and establish an information portal to track adaptation and mitigation objectives. The activity will provide technical assistance to the government in issuing resilience bonds, conducting feasibility studies to establish the maiden carbon market, and collaborating with private sector insurers to develop and improve index insurance for natural disasters. The private sector finance mobilized under this activity would be utilized for climate-resilience agriculture energy-efficient practices. The activity aligns with the priorities of the Government of Bangladesh in achieving its mitigation and adaptation targets. By strengthening Bangladesh's transformative capacity, the activity contributes to the U.S. Embassy's goal of making Bangladesh a socially and environmentally resilient country. Funding for the activity contributes to Adaptation-Indirect (300k), Global Food Security (500k), Private Sector Engagement ($150k) directives and key issues.

(Bangladesh): USAID's Tuberculosis (TB) Diagnostic Network Strengthening activity enhances the capacity of government and private sector laboratory systems to diagnose TB cases through equitable, accessible, rapid, and quality-assured testing. Using FY 2024 funds, the activity will support standardizing procedures and practices to meet the global quality standards for TB test results. Moreover, the activity will improve the laboratory information management systems and implement an optimized and reliable specimen transportation plan. The activity will also collaborate with private diagnostic networks to ensure that TB patients diagnosed in private laboratories adhere to national guidelines, meet international standards, and report patients to the national reporting system. The activity will closely collaborate with the National Tuberculosis Control Program to improve timely and accurate TB diagnosis; link confirmed cases to treatment services; reduce the spread of TB and preventable deaths; and contribute to global TB targets. The activity will have nationwide coverage, with an emphasis on underserved sections of the healthcare system. The activity will support the Joint Strategic Plan Goal Three, with the U.S. government's Integrated Country Strategy Mission Objective of Improving inclusive and equitable health, education, and livelihood services, especially for women, youth, and marginalized groups. The activity will advance the Indo-Pacific Strategy by working with GoB to intensify efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases.FY 2024 funding will contribute to SL Indirect ($700k), Digital Technology-Indirect ($250k), Innovation ($100k) Gender Equality ($500k), Health Workforce ($400k), PGI-Indirect Digital ($1.25m),PGI-Indirect Health ($1.45m) and PSE ($100k) issues.

title.narrative: Systems Strengthening for One Health Activity

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Systems Strengthening for One Health Activity prevents and counters the emergence of infectious disease outbreaks in Bangladesh, and enhances resilience against health-related shocks and stressors. This activity will support the building of a robust global health security architecture to prevent, detect, and respond to health threats at the animal, human, and environmental interface. To reduce the risk of pathogen spillover from domestic and wild animals to humans, this activity will build a collaborative multi-sectoral One Health system at the national and sub-national levels with the Ministries of Fisheries and Livestock; Environment, Forest, and Climate Change; and Health and Family Welfare. It will provide support to functionalize the One Health Secretariat as a multisectoral coordination mechanism. Using FY 2024 funds, the activity will support the government, communities of practices, and private sector to build robust systems to reduce the risk of antimicrobial resistance. It will build laboratory and surveillance systems to seamlessly share information and quickly detect and limit outbreaks. This activity will enhance the government and communities emergency operation and response capacity across the animal, human, and wildlife sectors. description.narrative: (Bangladesh): USAID's Chittagong Hill Tracts Watershed Co-Management Activity II (CHTWCA II) will build regional resilience through an integrated, inclusive ecosystem co-management approach that conserves the natural habitats and protects the wildlife of the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) watershed. The activity aligns with the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan and will advance the Indo-Pacific Strategy by mitigating threats to biodiversity, combating illegal logging and wildlife poaching, promoting environmental safeguards, fostering private sector engagement, and conserving ecosystems. The activity supports the U.S. government's objective of strengthening resilience to natural hazards and USAID's Climate Change Strategy. (Bangladesh): The FTF Bangladesh Sustainable Aquaculture Activity coordinates linkages among value chain actors across private, public, and civil society spheres. description.narrative: (Bangladesh): Using FY 2015 funds, the Protecting Human Rights (PHR) activity will continue its work to reduce domestic violence and child marriage and prevent violence against women including sexual harassment, and other human rights violations. To achieve these goals, the activity will train more than 8,000 Government of Bangladesh (GOB) officials, police, judges, lawyers, elected local representatives, teachers, and civil society organizations to improve their ability to prevent violence against women and child marriage. The activity will also organize educational and motivational sessions in 101 schools in USAID-assisted areas and provide 66 legal counselors to increase access to justice for survivors of domestic violence through alternate dispute resolution and formal legal proceedings. Finally, the PHR activity will support the GOB in adopting and enforcing comprehensive women's rights and domestic violence policies, including an amendment of the 1929 Child Marriage Restraint Act.

(Bangladesh): Using FY~2015 funds, the Marketing Innovations for Health (MIH) activity will continue its work to expand access to and the use of public health related products and services using a private-sector social marketing model. To accomplish that goal, MIH will provide training and technical assistance to improve the ability of local, private providers to deliver essential health and family planning services. To reinforce this marketing model, the activity will also improve knowledge and care seeking practices for newborn health and prevention of Acute Respiratory Infection through dissemination of best practices. Activities will also focus on youth through behavior change communication. The goal is to reach 2.1 million married women of reproductive age, 400,000 men, and 224,000 adolescent boys and girls with community-based education and behavior change activities.

(Bangladesh): This activity will continue the implementation of the Justice For All activity to improve delivery of legal aid in the formal justice sector, strengthen lower judiciary capacity, promote analysis of legal access, and increase citizen awareness of the rights exercised and enforced through formal justice institutions. The program will provide technical assistance and training for legal aid committees at the Supreme Court, district, and sub-district levels to improve the dissemination of information to citizens about available legal aid. USAID will develop and conduct culturally appropriate judicial training programs to introduce the 'International Framework for Court Excellence in the Judiciary of Bangladesh' through judicial system and policy reformation. This program provides legal support for poor and vulnerable people. By redressing their grievances, the program reduces their likelihood of being radicalized and increases their confidence in government institutions.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Agriculture Inputs Project improves the quality of agricultural outputs by increasing the availability and use of high quality, unadulterated agricultural inputs, such as good quality seeds and fertilizer. Using FY 2016 funds, the activity will continue to develop a network of private agricultural input retailers under an association model. The association will link producers, importers, wholesalers, and retailers and provide certifications on the quality of retail inputs. AIP will also develop trainings for retailers and provide support for selected certified retailers to establish or grow their business. AIP will also help establish the certified retailers as a source of information for farmers on up-to-date technologies and the effective use of inputs by linking the retailers to existing agriculture demonstration activities. Finally, AIP will assess the capacity of local organizations and agriculture input associations to support and advocate for certified retailers..

(Bangladesh): The Climate-Resilient Ecosystems and Livelihoods (CREL) activity increases the country's resilience to natural hazards through working with community-based organizations, government ministries and technical agencies. CREL provides technical assistance to the GOB and local communities to improve ecosystem conservation and resilience capacity through mitigating threats to biodiversity, reducing greenhouse gas emissions from deforestation and improper land use, sustainable management of forests and wetlands, and diversifying the livelihoods of people living in and near protected areas to reduce unsustainable exploitation of natural resources. CREL focuses on 21 forest protected areas, four wetlands and six ecologically critical areas. It will continue assisting the GOB to improve conservation policies and regulation.

(Bangladesh): With FY 2016 funds, the Agricultural Extension Capacity Building activity will continue its work to increase agricultural productivity and farm incomes through the formation of women and small farmer producer groups and by facilitating the linkage between those groups and extension services. The activity will achieve these goals by providing targeted technical assistance and training to farmers, producer groups, and extension agents. The activity will also develop a strategy to incorporate information, communication, and technology into extension services. For example, the activity will train farmers and extension agents to create and share their own extension products such as videos, podcasts, power point presentations, and web pages, allowing them to reach larger numbers of farmers with site-and crop-specific technical and commercial information. .

(Bangladesh): The goal of the ongoing SHIKHA activity is to improve maternal nutrition and infant and young child feeding practices in 26 sub-districts within the Feed the Future zone of influence through behavioral change communication. The activity will achieve this goal by training community health workers and public and private healthcare providers to conduct home visits and community forums during which they provide education and awareness raising on exclusive breastfeeding, appropriate food and feeding practices, and hand-washing with soap before preparing food and feeding children.

(Bangladesh): Winrock International, in partnership with Golden Harvest Agro Industries Limited, will continue to jointly implement the Cold Chain Bangladesh (CCB) Global Development Alliance (GDA) using FY2014 funds. This activity promotes economic growth and food security by developing Bangladesh's first integrated cold chain system, a network of refrigerated cold storage vehicles and facilities for selected value chain commodities. This will strengthen domestic food security by improving the preservation, storage and delivery of value-added food. In addition, the activity will increase income for farmers through reduction of waste and spoilage of harvested products. From a contribution of $5 million USAID leverages $10 million from Golden Harvest Agro Industries Limited.

(Bangladesh): USAID will invest FY 2016 funds in Sisimpur (the Bangladeshi version of Sesame Street), an educational television broadcast that reaches 12 million households weekly. As the most widely viewed children's television program in Bangladesh, the activity targets young children and their parents with content on health, nutrition, safety, the environment, gender equity, and social responsibility, in addition to lessons on literacy and numeracy. It thus reinforces the work of other Mission programs such as the Feed the Future and the Global Health Initiative while directly preparing pre-schoolers for school and fortifying the basic skills in children in early grades. The activity will continue to build the capacity of Sesame Workshop's branch in Bangladesh to independently manage, produce, and broadcast Sisimpur shows.

(Bangladesh): .Using FY 2016 funds, the Reading Enhancement for Advancing Development (READ) activity will continue to improve early grade reading in the lowest performing areas targeting 3.1 million students. Specifically, the activity trains primary school teachers to improve their teaching skills in reading. The READ activity will also conduct reading level assessments in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh. The assessment's results will shape strategies for providing regular feedback on reading achievement with the aim of increasing teachers' performance and increasing parents' involvement in their children's learning outside of the classroom. .

(Bangladesh): The Bengal Tiger Conservation Activity (Bagh) seeks to build a stronger and safer future for wild tigers and the local communities who rely upon their forest home - the Sundarbans. Through technical assistance and trainings, Bagh will increase the wildlife conservation knowledge base, reduce wildlife trafficking, minimize human-tiger conflict, generate alternative income opportunities for people living adjacent to the Sundarbans, and develop innovative and creative ways to promote tiger conservation to local, national and international audiences. Bagh will work with multiple national and international partners including the GOB, The Smithsonian, The German Government, Sundarbans communities, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector for high-level policy discussions on tiger conservation, combating wildlife crimes, and creative outreach activities to generate additional support from communities.

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): Advancing Adolescent Health (A2H) activity implements improved adolescent health and well-being by increasing access to, and utilization of, sexual and reproductive health services. Specifically, the A2H activity strengthens youth-friendly service provision at government health service sites and delivers both health information and life skills to unmarried adolescents. The activity will help strengthen input and seed systems, and incentivize crop diversification with rotational crops, such as value-added rice varieties, lentils, mustard, mung beans, and sunflowers, thereby increasing export volume and enabling higher returns to local firms and smallholder farmers. It will work with local market actors to generate business opportunities for US firms to collaborate with Bangladeshi companies and explore domestic market opportunities. The activity will provide training and resources that will build capacity of input suppliers to develop innovative marketing strategies so as to develop a loyal customer base. It will also build the capacity of supporting market actors, including financial service providers and business development service providers, with improved services and business models. To contribute to reducing the impact of COVID-19, the activity will strengthen or re-establish local markets by investing in key value chains; support mechanization and labor saving methods, due to potential labor shortages; identify other opportunities to increase the financial resilience of small and medium enterprises; and leverage existing information dissemination programs (e.g., extension and digital tools) to share critical COVID-19 messages...This activity will support the Global Food Security Strategy and significantly contribute to achieving the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal Two, the Indo-Pacific Strategy through private sector engagement, and U.S. government's mission objective of improved food security in Bangladesh

title.narrative: Advancing Women’s Right of Access to Information in Bangladesh

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .USAID/Bangladesh will promote freedom of information to fight corruption in Bangladesh. The activity will increase citizen capacity to file requests for non-controversial data to enhance government transparency. As corruption flourishes in secrecy, any progress towards transparent and open government advances anti-corruption efforts. The activity will provide training to female citizens on how to access information held by the government, as well as how to work in their communities to raise awareness of the impediments faced by women who attempt to exercise their right to information...The activity also will work with civil-society organizations that focus on women's rights and economic empowerment to raise women's awareness of the 2009 Right to Information Act (RTI), assist women in filing information requests, and advocate to improve the government's response to requests for information. The activity will partner with Government of Bangladesh's relevant ministries to train information officers to reduce gender inequalities in information-dissemination and to enhance their capacity to implement the RTI. The activity will promote gender-sensitive implementation of RTI to make government open to public scrutiny, advancing anti-corruption efforts. Through increased transparency of service delivery and knowledge of how to hold the government accountable through RTI, USAID will increase citizen confidence in governance institutions...This activity was selected through a competitive process to support citizen, and especially women's access to host-government information. This activity reduces corruption and directly supports the U.S. National Security Strategy, the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal Two, and U.S. Government's mission objective of increasing citizen confidence in governance institutions in Bangladesh... ...

title.narrative: Marketing Innovations for Sustainable Health Development

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The Marketing Innovations for Sustainable Health Development activity continues to meet market demand for family planning, health, and nutrition products and services through its service and distribution networks. USAID helped establish the Social Marketing Company (SMC) in 1974 - now a sustainable local organization with over $150 million in annual revenue. Since 2016, USAID's partnership with SMC has been through a Global Development Alliance that currently leverages $17 USD for every $1 USD spent by USAID. Using FY 2024 funds, SMC will utilize its vast network of sales agents and service delivery outlets to deliver public health products. The network includes private physicians, pharmacists, non-graduate medical practitioners, and rural female community sales agents. This network will deliver services such as growth monitoring and promotion for children under five; nutrition counseling; counseling to delay early marriage and pregnancy; and referring gender-based violence survivors to care centers. Network providers will sell SMC-branded commodities such as contraceptives; oral rehydration salts; maternal and child micronutrient products; safe delivery kits; menstrual hygiene products; electrolyte drinks; and micronutrient fortified biscuits. SMC will create new private sector partnerships to expand its products and services, eventually ending its reliance on USAID funds. The activity supports goal three of the Joint Strategic Plan and ICS Mission Objective three. The activity will advance the Indo-Pacific Strategy by working with GoB to intensify efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases.FY 2024 funding will contribute to Adaptation Indirect ($250k), Innovation (200k), Gender Equality ($1.2m), GBV ($100k),GBV-CEFM ($200k), GFS ($400k), Cross-Cutting HSS ($250k), MHPSS($150k), MSN ($400k), Macronutrients ($300k of which Vit A is $200k), PGI-Indirect Health ($1.5m), PSE ($400k) and WASH ($50k) issues.

With FY 2020 funds, Ujjiban will intensify its focus on gender and health by using diverse communication media and methods (both traditional and new) as well as community outreach programs to encourage audience members to adopt key health behaviors in the areas of maternal, neonatal and child health; family planning, tuberculosis, and nutrition. The activity will further explore opportunities to leverage the private sector to ensure greater coverage of Ujjiban's SBCC products. (Bangladesh): The Strengthening Political Landscape (SPL) activity strengthens the skills of political party members and citizens; advocates for more inclusive party policies and practices; and mitigates intra- and inter- party conflict. The SPL activity is designed to train political leaders with conflict mitigation skills, to enhance their leadership abilities, and promote gender equality and democratic inclusiveness. The consolidation of power by the Awami League has left limited political space for opposition political parties to participate in political public debate. In this context, the SPL activity provides a platform for political party members to participate in multi-party dialogues, both on social and traditional media platforms, where they can openly express their views on current political issues. USAID will conduct fellowship training programs for young and senior political leaders to develop leadership and political skills, and to assist in building political parties based on democratic principles and practices. The activity will also focus on training women in order to achieve the 33 percent quota for women's representation in all political party committees. USAID will continue to utilize digital platforms to ensure political parties are able to produce and broadcast digital events, and to develop digital databases to increase their ability to recruit online members. The activity will train candidates on electoral rules, electoral codes of conduct and campaign management, and conduct other elections activity in the next fiscal year. The activity will contribute to "Freedom of Expression" ($1.6m) and GBV($787,500) and GBV-CEFM($787,500) earmark. This activity is in line with the State-USAID Integrated Country Strategy (ICS) Mission Goal Two and the U.S. government development objective of "Improved Democratic Systems that Promote Transparency, Accountability, and Integrity."

(Bangladesh): The Research for Decision Makers (RDM) activity will support implementation research on priority health areas, provide advisory services to the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) to guide health policy and strategy formulation, and build health-sector research capacity. description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .The Improving Nutrition through Community-based Approaches activity is designed to improve communities' knowledge of nutritional requirements during the first one thousand days of life (from conception to 24 months of age), and increase access to and use of health and nutrition services at targeted health facilities. The activity addresses high levels of stunting and malnutrition in 11 priority sub-districts across three districts. The activity trains and supports Community Nutrition Promoters to reach '1000-day' households with counseling on infant feeding and care practices. In addition to household visits, the Community Nutrition Promoters provide community and family support through sessions with mothers, fathers, mothers-in-law, and adolescents. The activity improves the quality of nutrition services by training providers in nutrition and building the capacity of established community clinic management groups to advocate for support from district health officials...This activity is aligned with Agency-wide objectives under Global Health such as Preventing Child and Maternal Deaths. Undernutrition is estimated to be an underlying cause of 45 percent of child mortality and anemia contributes to 20 percent of maternal mortality. Thus, investing in nutrition is fundamental to achieving the goals of the Call to Action and Sustainable Development Goals. This project contributes to United States government's support of the 2025 World Health Assembly targets for nutrition...This activity is also designed as a tool to enhance the knowledge, and increase access to and use of health and nutrition services. The activity supports the U.S. National Security Strategy, the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal Two, and the U.S. Government's mission objective of improved health status in Bangladesh..

(Bangladesh): The Integrated Agriculture and Health Based Interventions (IAHBI) activity will improve household food security and nutritional status, focusing on mothers and young children in the southern region of Bangladesh. The activity will increase the quantity and variety of foods available, with special emphasis on foods rich in micronutrients. In addition, the activity will enhance the intake of adequate and diversified diets among young children, women of child-bearing age, and households through homestead and community food production. The activity promotes the use of a variety of locally available food sources including horticulture, fish and poultry. Finally, the activity will improve coverage of nutrition interventions, such as iron and folic acid supplementation, deworming, hand washing and sanitation.

Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change. (Bangladesh): The new Environment, Health & Safety (EHS+) Center in Bangladesh activity will help drive the uptake of safe, clean and climate friendly practices in Bangladesh's clothing export industry. The export sector of Bangladesh is anchored by the ready-made garment industry. This Global Development Alliance (GDA), proposed by Institute of Sustainable Communities (ISC), will establish a Bangladesh-owned and operated EHS+ Center that will address the root causes of the prevailing issues in export-oriented garments factories. The EHS+ Center will be established in the North South University in Dhaka - ISC's local partner in Bangladesh. The Center will provide training to factory engineers, line workers, plant managers and owners so that factory personnel can apply this knowledge in their workplace and promote sustainable industrial practices that will improve factory performance in health and safety, environmental management, resource efficiency, energy and carbon management. The EHS+ Center will provide 24 international-standard, technical courses in energy management, energy efficiency, and energy auditing to provide Bangladesh managers with the skills they need to reduce energy consumption of factories.

The activity's primary beneficiaries are primary school students, teachers, and primary school inspectors..

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF) flight services will continue to support USAID and its partner agencies to access hard-to-reach areas in Bangladesh, safely and efficiently ensuring that development interventions benefit everyone, including those in remote areas who are usually the most vulnerable. In Bangladesh, many areas that are prone to poverty and climate change are difficult to access on foot and as such, aerial photographs are vital to study and map them. This activity will include an aerial survey facility to support USAID decision-making by providing easily accessible GPS tagged aerial photographs over vulnerable and high-risk areas. These aerial surveys will also include locations to assist USAID and its partners in documenting the impact of slow-onset events such as riverbank erosion and waterlogging to help chart population movements, loss of agricultural land, etc. Through chartered and shuttle flights, MAF will continue its flight services to all development and humanitarian agencies working to save human life and improve the livelihoods of vulnerable people in Bangladesh. MAF flight services will help increase the chances of aid agencies accessing hard-to-reach areas towards ensuring that no one is left behind. MAF will contribute to activity monitoring oversight, needs assessment, joint missions with other development partners and private sector organizations where it is hard to reach. It will provide flight services to anywhere in Bangladesh where commercial flights are unavailable or multiple vehicles are necessary to reach, and will continue to focus on the areas of emergency and disaster responses, food security, climate change, natural resource management, energy, health, education, and population. In addition, MAF services may contribute to emergency services for medical supplies, including COVID test kits and lab reagents and for training of service providers in remote public health facilities.. .

title.narrative: Chittagong Hill Tracts Watershed Co-Management Activity (CHTWCA)

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): This activity builds regional resilience through an integrated, inclusive ecosystem co-management approach that conserves the natural habitats and protects the wildlife of the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) watershed. It provides technical assistance to the Forest Department, Ministry of CHT Affairs, Hill District Councils, Village Common Forest Management Committees, local civil society partners and forest-dependent communities. The activity implements the GoB's approved Integrated Watershed Management Action Plan and conducts natural regeneration surveys to inform forest baseline status and utilize geographic information systems mapping to identify suitable micro-watersheds for assisted natural regeneration activities in the forest reserves. With FY 2022 funds, the activity will continue to raise awareness of forest and wildlife crimes; provide training on climate change adaptation, sustainable forest management, and social cohesion; and advance market-linked resilient livelihoods. Social cohesion activities will help mediate land tenure and communal conflict among host communities affected by Rohingya migration. The activity will sequester or reduce greenhouse emissions by improving the management of targeted forests and wetlands. Environmental degradation and climate change intensifies the impacts of water insecurity, floods and storms in the CHT. Protection of forests will prevent landslides and contribute to long-term ecosystem services for food, water, and livelihoods, and thus supports the U.S. government's objective of strengthening resilience to natural hazards. Funding for this activity will contribute to meeting the required Host Community ($1,000,000), Microenterprise and Livelihoods ($500,000), and Gender Based Violence ($250,000) directives. $300,000 of Biodiversity funds will be attributed to Adaptation Indirect.

title.narrative: Institutionalization of Food Safety in Bangladesh for Safer Food

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .The Government of Bangladesh (GOB) identified food safety as a priority with the passage of the 2013 Food Safety Act and the creation of the Bangladesh Food Safety Authority (BFSA). BFSA is responsible for developing science-based regulations and coordinating all food safety activities within the 18 Bangladeshi line ministries and 450 district offices for enforcing food safety laws. A science based regulatory agency is also a necessary step to encourage private sector investment in the potentially lucrative agriculture sector in Bangladesh. Focused activities will include: support GOB to operationalize the BFSA management board, develop BFSA organizational structure and performance standards, standardize food lab processes, and create a template for writing food safety regulations. Recently, the BFSA received authority to hire 350 key leadership staff positions, including laboratory and training teams. Operationalizing activities will include training, capacity building activities with key leaders, including the 350 to-be hired, associated agencies, and working to bring the private sector into the food safety regulatory realm. FAO, with technical guidance from USAID, will conduct technical capacity building workshops with key members of the Bangladesh Food Safety Board and private sector actors. These workshops will focus on developing food policy, strategy for future growth, and key science-based regulations. FAO will usher through the legislative process these key regulations which will be translated into laws. The activity will also help create a 4-year Bachelor Degree program in Food Management at Bangladesh Agriculture University. This will be the first of its kind program in the region...The activity supports the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goals Two and Three, the U.S. Indo-Pacific Strategy, and the U.S. Government's mission objectives of improved food security in Bangladesh and increased fair and reciprocal trade and investment..

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .The Strengthening Forest Monitoring in Bangladesh activity will expand the Government of Bangladesh's (GOB) use of innovative forest monitoring technologies. (Bangladesh): .The Meeting the Undernutrition Challenge (MUCH) activity will strengthen the enabling environment for eradicating food insecurity and malnutrition by providing policy advice and strengthening the capacity of government and relevant stakeholders in order to develop national food security and nutrition (FSN) policy frameworks, country investment plan (CIP) and strategies. The implementer will achieve this outcome through offering specialized FSN training courses, including enrolment of government officials in post-graduate programs. To implement, monitor and assess impacts of policies and strategies on FSN aligned with the national food policy and the CIP, the implementor will provide monitoring training, and conduct a series of multi-sectoral and multi-stakeholder consultations engaging 17 Ministries and Departments as well as CSOs and the private sector. The MUCH activity will generate updated information of food consumption and dietary diversity; such as the Food Insecurity Experience Scale which provides data for monitoring the Sustainable Development Goal Two of No Hunger; through a household survey, data verification workshops, and technical consultations. The implementor will develop a map of the extent and severity of chronic food insecurity at the sub-national level through updated FSN data collection at sub-national level as well as Integrated Food security Phase Classification assessments...FAO is a global leader in the food security sector and has a very strong relationship with the Ministry of Food. description.narrative: (Bangladesh): The new USAID Agricultural Biotechnology Support Project II (ABSP II) addresses key constraints in crop productivity, enhances crop diversification, promotes food security, and furthers environmental goals. description.narrative: (Bangladesh): .The USAID Obirodh -- Road to Tolerance activity strengthens community, civil society, and government capacity to resist violent extremism in Bangladesh. This activity works with civil society to train parents, teachers, local government, and peer and community leaders to identify signs of radicalization and prevent recruitment into violent extremist organizations. Funds will be used to help civil society engage these main target group and strategic group in CVE interventions, as well as to commission new research. This activity was selected as the most-direct method to engage civil society and communities in activities with the potential to prevent radicalization within a learning framework. This acitivity supports Pillar One of the U.S. National Security Strategy, "Defending U.S. National Security," the State-USAID Joint Strategic Plan Goal One, and U.S. government's mission objective of CVE in Bangladesh..

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): SHOUHARDO III works with targeted communities to support their food security through integrated activities designed to improve their livelihoods, health, hygiene, nutrition, and resilience, while expanding women's empowerment. The activities will also improve the health and nutritional status of all, especially pregnant and nursing women, adolescent girls, and children under five, through education and communications, by creating a corps of community nutrition advisors who are self-supporting through sales of nutrition and hygiene products. SHOUHARDO III activities will also support disaster mitigation through the raising of house plints, building awareness for slope protection in schools, earthen mounds and embankments by planting vegetation, and training of communities. SHOUHARDO III will support the existing transformative groups as change agents for achieving gender equality and promoting early childhood care and development. It will continue enhancing the capacity of government institutions and community associations to empower the women and the vulnerable and help them to exercise their rights through active participation in development activities. This activity supports the U.S. government's objectives to provide improved quality of life opportunities and enhance the people's lives to create a healthy, self-sufficient, resilient and sustainable economy in Bangladesh which supports the country's journey to self-reliance.. .

Support facility-based and outreach services, improving the quality and equitable coverage of antenatal, delivery and postpartum care services, including periodic evaluation of the progress of pregnancy, labor support, use of the partogram, clean delivery, and active management of the third stage of labor.
